speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to evaluate the cause of your acute diarrhea. How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and how many times per day are you passing loose stools?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mention you were recently treated for pneumonia with levofloxacin; given your history of high-volume watery diarrhea and abdominal cramping, are you experiencing any fever, chills, blood in your stool, or signs of dehydration such as dizziness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Levofloxacin-associated Clostridioides difficile infection (C. diff colitis).

Given the recent fluoroquinolone use and high-volume watery diarrhea with cramping, I am requesting stool testing for C. diff toxins and a CBC to assess for leukocytosis.
